---
title: Contribute a notebook
---

The [examples gallery](../examples/index.qmd) collects notebooks that each
read the composite for one place and set it next to other data for that
place. You add one through a pull request. The
[Pergamino tutorial](../tutorials/pergamino.qmd) is the reference example:
read it before you start, and reuse its structure where it fits.

The guidance on this page describes what makes a notebook easy to review and
to keep running. None of it is a hard rule. Where your notebook departs from
it, say why in the notebook itself.

## Choose the data

Prefer sources that publish in cloud-optimized formats, which let a notebook
read the area of interest without downloading whole files:

- [Cloud-optimized GeoTIFF](https://cogeo.org/) for rasters, such as this
  dataset's [STAC catalog](https://data.source.coop/nlebovits/landsat-lst/catalog.json).
- [GeoParquet](https://geoparquet.org/) for vector data, such as
  [Overture Maps buildings](https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/buildings/).
- [PMTiles](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/) for map tiles.
- [Zarr](https://zarr.dev/) for multidimensional arrays.
- [STAC](https://stacspec.org/) catalogs that index any of these formats.

[Source Cooperative](https://source.coop/) hosts several datasets that pair
well with surface temperature, such as the
[Global Human Settlement Layer](https://source.coop/nlebovits/ghsl) and the
[Meta and WRI canopy height map](https://source.coop/tge-labs/meta-chm-v2).
The [intended use](../about/intended-use.qmd) page lists more ancillary data.

If the data you need comes only as a Shapefile or a zipped download, you can
still use it. Explain the exception in
a sentence near the cell that reads it.

## Limit the run time

CI executes every notebook on a standard GitHub-hosted runner. Aim for about
10 minutes of run time, and treat 25 minutes as the limit, because the job
times out there.

- Read only the area of interest. Pass a bounding box or a window to every
  read, and never load a whole 5-degree tile when you need one city.
- Choose one city or region, not a country.
- Cache nothing outside the repository. A notebook that depends on a file in
  your home directory fails in CI.

## Lay out the folder

Each example has its own folder under `docs/examples/`. Use a short,
lowercase slug for the folder name, such as the city:

```text
docs/examples/<slug>/
├── index.qmd        # the notebook
└── thumbnail.png    # the gallery image, about 800 x 500 px
```

Write the notebook as a Quarto document with Python cells rather than as an
`.ipynb` file. Quarto stores the outputs in `docs/_freeze/`, and
a reviewer reads plain text.

## Write the front matter

The gallery builds each card from the notebook's front matter. Copy this
template into the top of `index.qmd` and fill in every field:

```yaml
---
title: "Surface heat and tree canopy in <place>"
author: "<Your name>"
date: "<YYYY-MM-DD>"
description: >-
  One or two sentences on the question the notebook answers, and for which
  place.
categories:
  - <Place, Country>
  - Landsat LST P95
  - <Each other dataset the notebook reads>
image: thumbnail.png
---
```

Use the place and every dataset as categories. Readers filter the gallery by
them, and a dataset name that matches an existing card groups the two.

## Write the notebook

- Start with the question the notebook answers and the place it covers.
  Follow it with the data, the analysis, and what the result means for a
  planning decision.
- The site folds code by default. Each cell shows its output and hides its
  source behind a toggle. Write the prose around the cells so a reader can
  follow the notebook without opening them.
- Reuse the plotting helpers in `docs/_plotting.py` to give your figures the
  same look as the rest of the site. Quarto runs each notebook from its own
  folder. Put `docs/` on the import path from there:

  ```python
  import sys
  from pathlib import Path

  sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parents[1]))
  import _plotting
  ```

- State units and the decode rule where you convert the composite's integer
  values to degrees Celsius.
- Keep the prose clean for [Vale](https://vale.sh/). The repository's
  [prose rules](https://github.com/nlebovits/landsat-lst-pipeline/blob/main/docs/PROSE.md)
  apply to notebooks, and CI checks them at error level.

If the notebook needs a Python package that the project does not declare yet,
add it to the `docs` dependency group in the same pull request:

```bash
uv add --group docs <package>
```

## Render and commit

Run these commands from the repository root to execute your notebook and then
render the whole site the way CI does:

```bash
uv sync --group docs
uv run --group docs quarto render \
  docs/examples/<slug>/index.qmd --execute
uv run --group docs quarto render docs
```

Preview the result while you edit:

```bash
uv run --group docs quarto preview docs
```

Then check the prose:

```bash
vale --minAlertLevel=error \
  docs/examples/<slug>/index.qmd
```

Rendering writes the notebook's outputs to `docs/_freeze/examples/<slug>/`.
Commit that directory with the notebook. The docs workflow renders the site
from the committed freeze. If a notebook's source no longer matches its
freeze, the render executes the notebook again, and the workflow fails because
`docs/_freeze/` changed.

Quarto compares only the notebook's own source with its freeze. A notebook
also reads `docs/_plotting.py`, the fonts in `docs/fonts/`, and the other
files in its own directory, such as a data file. The file
`docs/_notebook_inputs.json` records a hash of those inputs for each
notebook, and the docs workflow fails when one no longer matches. After you
change an input, execute the notebook again and update the record:

```bash
uv run --group docs quarto render \
  docs/examples/<slug>/index.qmd --execute
python3 .github/scripts/docs_notebooks.py record
```

Commit the refreshed freeze and `docs/_notebook_inputs.json` together.

## Open the pull request

Open a pull request against `main`, and fill in the template's fields for the
data sources, the run time on your machine, and the refreshed freeze. When a pull request changes a notebook, CI executes that
notebook from a clean freeze, and a cell that raises an error fails the
check. After the merge, a weekly run executes every notebook again and opens
an issue if one of them breaks.

To discuss an idea before you write it, open a
[notebook proposal](https://github.com/nlebovits/landsat-lst-pipeline/issues/new?template=notebook-proposal.yml).
